record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the boundary value problem -Δu + 1/u^α = λ f(x) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where α > 0 (mainly α < 1) and f ≥ 0, does there exist, in addition to the known maximal positive solution for sufficiently large λ, any further solution that is either another positive solution or a compact-support (free-boundary) solution?

evidence.quote: -Δu + 1/u^α = λ f(x) in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, where 0 < α (mainly α < 1) and f ≥ 0.
but it remains the problem of the possible existence of more solutions, either positive or with compact support.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \geq 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $\alpha > 0$ (with the principal interest in the range $0 < \alpha < 1$), and let $f \in L^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfy $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$. For a parameter $\lambda > 0$, consider the singular semilinear boundary value problem
$$-\Delta u + \frac{1}{u^\alpha} = \lambda f(x) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
where the term $1/u^\alpha$ is interpreted as $0$ on the set $\{u = 0\}$ (so that solutions may be either strictly positive in $\Omega$ or nonnegative with a free boundary $\partial\{u > 0\} \cap \Omega$).

It is known that for all sufficiently large $\lambda$ there exists a maximal positive solution $u_\lambda \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ satisfying $u_\lambda > 0$ in $\Omega$.

Question: For such $\lambda$, does the problem admit, in addition to the maximal positive solution, any further solution — either another strictly positive solution, or a nonnegative solution with compact support in $\Omega$ (i.e., a free boundary solution vanishing on a set of positive measure)?
artifact.category_tag: singular semilinear elliptic equations with absorption
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related work on branches of positive and free-boundary solutions to singular quasilinear elliptic problems, and on multiplicity results for related singular equations, but no source was found that conclusively settles the existence (or non-existence) of a second positive solution or a compact-support free-boundary solution beyond the maximal positive solution for the specific problem $-\Delta u + u^{-\alpha} = \lambda f(x)$ with $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$. The status therefore appears to remain unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Branches of positive and free boundary solutions for some singular quasilinear elliptic problems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence and multiplicity of strictly positive or nonnegative solutions with a free boundary for one-dimensional quasilinear singular eigenvalue-type problems.
status_evidence.claim: Related branches of positive and free-boundary solutions are studied, but the multiplicity question for the multidimensional semilinear problem is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Convexity for free boundaries with singular term (nonlinear elliptic case)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geometric properties of free boundaries arising in singular elliptic problems.
status_evidence.claim: Free-boundary aspects of singular elliptic problems are an active topic, without a definitive multiplicity statement for the stated problem.
